newsitem.title: USA: ABC says CFO Doerfler to resign.
newsitem.headline: ABC says CFO Doerfler to resign.

text.p: Walt Disney Co's ABC Inc unit said Monday that Ronald Doerfler, its chief financial officer, is resigning.
No replacement was named. "(President) Bob Iger would hope to name someone in the coming weeks," a spokesman said.
ABC said Doerfler would remain in the post through January 1998.
In a statement, Iger said Doerfler indicated he would "seek out new, challenging opportunities to create shareholder value" at another company.
In an interview, Doerfler said he has not been approached by another company about a specific job. He said he would seek a job "probably as the CFO of a public company."
While there was "probably a greater possibility" he would go to another media or entertainment company, CFO skills "are fairly transferable" and can be used in other industries.
He began considering a job change shortly after the merger of Capital Cities/ABC and Walt Disney Co in 1995, saying that, after the deal, he was insufficiently challenged.
He said there was a certain inevitability to his leaving after the deal, since a parent company now oversaw ABC.
He would seek a job at a company with good growth opportunities, calling his impending departure "extraordinarily amicable. Everybody has been terrific about it."
He added that he will remain in the post "long enough to make sure things don't fall through cracks."
